newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTOR RACING-SAUBER LEAD CHASE FOR WURZ.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SAUBER LEAD CHASE FOR WURZ.

text.p: Formula One newcomer Alexander Wurz gave his career a major boost at Silverstone by completing his third gand prix in third place.

The Austrian's manager Peter Cramer said on Monday the Benetton test driver, who replaced compatriot Gerhard Berger in the last three races, had received an offer from the Sauber team as well as "inquiries for next year from other top teams."
"We have the possibility to join Sauber this year already. Within the next few days we have to think about contract conditions," Cramer said, adding that Benetton had no objections.
According to Cramer, Wurz will be competing in the German Grand Prix at Hockenheim in two weeks either for Benetton, should Berger remain absent, or for Sauber.
"Third place in only my third race is not bad is it? This has definately helped my career enormously," said Wurz after his performance at Sunday's British Grand Prix.
Wurz had little time to celebrate as he was due to test for Benetton in Monza on Monday. "I can't get into the cockpit on Monday if I'm tired," he said.
"This result is wonderful, I think I am entitled to be proud of myself, but I do still have to digest it all."
Wurz, who failed to finish in his two previous grands prix, admitted to having had a few scary moments on Sunday when he felt he would slide off the track.
"At the beginning I had a lot of oversteer because the car was so heavy. During the safety car phase my tyres were very slippery," he said.

When asked if Benetton had ordered him not to overtake team mate Jean Alesi, who finished just ahead of the Austrian, Wurz replied: "At first I did want to overtake him, but then after my pit stop I decided I would complete the race in third place.
"I even told the team not to worry. I wouldn't be launching an attack on Alesi."
